To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the length–force behavior of obliquely striped, mitochondrial poor, circular muscle fibers in squid varies as a function of radial position in the wall of the mantle.

the contractile properties of the CMP circular muscle of Doryteuthiis pealeii vary transmurally, with the fibers near the inner mantle wall producing higher force output at all points along ascending limb of the muscle length–tension relationship.
the length–tensile force and operating length range vary transmurally within the circular muscle of squid mantle.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the contractile properties of obliquely striped muscles vary transmurally within a cylindrical muscular organ, and how this variation in contractile properties is related to the mechanical properties and functional demands of the muscle.
the functional diversity of the obliquedly striated, central, mitochondria-poor muscle fibers of the squid mantle, which is an example of a hollow, cylindrical muscular organ.
the mechanical properties of the squid mantle muscle, which is a model for understanding the mechanical properties of other muscular hydrostats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the length–tensile force behavior of the CMP circular muscle in the mantle of squid varies transmurally and that this variation may be important for the function of this muscle during locomotion and escape jetting.
the obliquely-striated, circular fibers of the squid mantle wall exhibit significant variation in contractile properties with respect to radial position in the wall.

the length–tensile force behavior and the operating range of the squid mantle wall are transmurally heterogeneous, and that this is an adaptation to the non-uniform strain environment in which the mantle muscle operates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the squid mantle is a complex muscular organ that is designed to operate over a wide range of muscle lengths and strains, and to produce large forces at short muscle lengths.
obliquely striating the CMP fibers in the squid mantle provides the muscle with an effective way to increase the operating range of the length–force relationship.
the CMP circular fibers are capable of producing higher forces at a given muscle length than fibers from the same muscle that operate near the outer surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obliquely striate muscles can be highly variable in their mechanical properties, even when the fibers are from the same muscle and are of similar size and orientation.

the CMP circular fibers near both the inner and outer surface of the squid mantle operate along the ascending limb, and the fibers near the inner mantle wall operate at a shorter optimal length and produce more force at that length than the fibers near the outer mantle wall.

the CMP muscle fibers in the mantle wall of D. pealeii are not uniform in contractile properties, but rather vary in their length–tension properties transmurally, with fibers near the inner mantle surface being more powerful than fibers near the outer mantle surface.
